hook: How a $299 robot actually washes its own mop. No, really.

scenes.visual_prompt: Robot vacuum driving back toward its dock after a cleaning run, dock lit up and ready
scenes.on_screen_text: The dock is the entire value prop
scenes.voiceover: At this price point, the dock is the entire reason to buy — so let's actually look at what it does.

scenes.visual_prompt: Macro cutaway animation of the dock base washing mop pads with hot water jets
scenes.voiceover: After a run, the robot docks and the base washes the mop pads with hot water.

scenes.visual_prompt: Animation of rollers wringing a wet mop pad, water draining into the base
scenes.voiceover: Then it wrings them with rollers instead of leaving them sopping wet.

scenes.visual_prompt: Warm air vents blowing visible heat waves over the mop pads inside the dock, timer graphic showing a few hours
scenes.on_screen_text: Step 3: warm-air dry, a few hours
scenes.voiceover: Warm air dries them, usually over a few hours, before the next cycle.

scenes.visual_prompt: Side-by-side comparison: a damp, slightly discolored mop pad next to a fully dried clean pad, with a small odor-wave graphic over the damp one
scenes.voiceover: Skip or underpower that drying step, and a damp mop pad is the single biggest source of sour smell in cheap wet-dry robots.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand wiping down a sticky kitchen floor with a bottle of floor cleaner before setting the robot loose
scenes.voiceover: One thing the dock won't fix: ground-in sticky residue. Do a manual deep clean before you hand off maintenance to the robot.

scenes.visual_prompt: Clean floor, robot resting quietly at dock, blog link icon overlay
scenes.on_screen_text: Full mechanism breakdown on the blog
scenes.voiceover: Every detail on how this cycle works is in the full post, linked in bio.

caption: The self-cleaning dock is the whole reason this category jumped from $900+ to $299 — so I broke down exactly what happens in that wash-wring-dry cycle, and the one failure mode (damp pads = smell) that reviewers flag most. Full post linked in bio.
